line: Had the iceberg tucked on my waist (Bling)
vault_lines: Had the iceberg tucked in my waist (Bling)
meaning:
He wants you to know that he was ready to go. He had the “iceberg”, that which earlier he called a “paperweight”, aka a diamond engagement ring, stashed in his waistband (a good spot to put something you want to keep both concealed and easily accessible). After hearing her responses when he brings up marriage, he realizes they want different things out of the relationship. He does not propose to her, leaving the ring stashed hidden in the waistband.

Alternatively, “iceberg” could be an oblique reference to his penis, if it (his penis) was erect and he decided to tuck it into his waistband to conceal that fact.

line: Let me get this paperweight
vault_lines: Let me get this paperweight, then come be my wife
meaning: He’s talking about an engagement ring. Gemstones are shiny rocks, and a big heavy rock can be used as a paperweight, so it’s sounds like he’s going for a big expensive diamond engagement ring.

line: The reason that you suffer is desire (Huh)
vault_lines: The reason that you suffer is desire (Huh)
meaning:
Probably from the Four Noble Truths of Buddhism, which are as stated:


Suffering, pain, and misery exist in life
Suffering arises from attachment to desires
Suffering ceases when attachment to desire ceases
Freedom from suffering is possible by practicing the Eightfold Path

line: (I might let you go)
vault_lines: I might let you go
meaning: This snippet from a song that was “put on the radio” is snipped from Ink’s outro to this very song. With this, Glover foreshadows the breakup at the end of the song. Bino turns on the radio to escape the “awkwardness” of realizing the girl he is with has had various struggles with love in her life, from her parents' split to the books on her shelf that deal with love in the modern world. She has “a whole lot of ride” on her, which could be related to the emotional baggage she has accumulated.

line: This ain’t special, tell me what you want This ain’t special, baby, this is fun This ain’t special, tell me what you want This ain’t special, baby, this is fun
vault_lines: This ain't special, tell me what you want
meaning:
The bridge is presumably from the perspective of the woman Glover raps/sings about on the first verse. She expresses that their relationship is not anything special or serious.

Throughout the first verse, it’s implied that the woman isn’t as serious about the relationship as Glover, who seems to admit that he has fallen in love. When Glover tells her “come be my wife,” she responds with:

You don’t understand what this is (Oh wait, wait, wait, wait)
I ain’t lookin' for another lifetime
Let’s just stay here and enjoy the great design

line: Then come be my wife She just laughed and touched my face (What you mean?) You don’t understand what this is (Oh, wait, wait, wait, wait) I ain’t lookin’ for another lifetime Let’s just stay here and enjoy the great design
vault_lines: She just laughed and touched my face (What you mean?)
meaning:
Throughout this verse, it’s implied that the woman isn’t as serious about the relationship as Glover.

When Glover suggests marriage, she first laughs it off. She is however very honest about what she wants out of the relationship. The woman expresses that she doesn’t want to get into a committing relationship, especially a commitment as big as marriage. She tells him to just enjoy the time they have together, and live in the moment.

The theme of “living in the moment” is explored throughout the album. On the chorus of “47.48,” Glover sings:

Don’t worry ‘bout tomorrow

line: Lay back on my back (Uh), vibrate
vault_lines: Lay back on my back (Uh), vibrate
meaning:
This could be a reference to “Vibrate” by André 3000. This whole song seems to take inspiration from André’s unique style from The Love Below. Aside from the 3 Stacks inspired flow, Gambino is also using the same tone to sing.

DJ Dahi, who co-produced the song, remarked the song’s similarities with The Love Below in a Rolling Stone interview:

It ended up having kind of The Love Below energy — funky, odd, but feels good.

It’s also a literal reference to Glover’s phone vibrating. The phone keeps getting blown up with calls by his ex-lover.

line: Got a girl in Harvard, I talk proper when I call her (21)
vault_lines: Got a girl in Harvard, I talk proper when I call her (21)
meaning:
Harvard is a private Ivy League research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It is widely regarded as one of the most prestigious universities in the world. As 21’s girl is “in Harvard” it is then reasonable to assume that she must be very intelligent; 21 thus makes sure to adopt an appropriately intelligent or “proper” manner of speech when he calls her.

Coincidentally, Childish Gambino (Donald Glover) was the subject of a 2018-2019 supplemental essay question for another Ivy League school, Dartmouth College:

Emmy and Grammy winner Donald Glover is a 21st century Renaissance man—an actor, comedian, writer, director, producer, singer, songwriter, rapper, and DJ. And yet the versatile storyteller and performer recently told an interviewer, “The thing I imagine myself being in the future doesn’t exist yet.” Can you relate?

line: Most these niggas wanna run around with these SZAs (Yeah) I prefer to just stroll the park with this Chaka
vault_lines: Most these niggas wanna run around with these SZAs (Yeah)
meaning:
Gambino employs a play-on-words with ‘scissors’ (because of the classic precautionary saying “don’t run with scissors”) and the TDE singer SZA. This also connects with the next line in its reference to the famous R&B/soul singer Chaka Khan.

His reference to SZA here shouldn’t be too surprising as he himself was found running around with the singer in her music video for the song “Garden (Say It Like Dat).”

line: Then I turned to a dirty look, uh (Meow) Ayy, why your cat lookin’ at me sideways? “Sing to her” I said, “Nah, I’ll put on the radio, though”
vault_lines: Then I turned to a dirty look, uh (Meow)
meaning:
In this line, Bino uses the word “cat” as a euphemism for her vagina, which is most commonly referred to as “pussy” in many other rap songs.

Due to the psychedelics he took earlier he begins hallucinating and imagines an anthropomorphic exchange with her vagina, in which it tells him to “sing to her”, another euphemism, this time referring to cunnilingus.



Bino hesitates and chooses to play the radio instead.

line: Someone made a mess in my account (Someone sound like me, yes) Someone bought a Patek in a panic (Yes, yes) Bode, Bentley addict, I go manic (Oh no)
vault_lines: Someone made a mess in my account (Someone sound like me, yes)
meaning:
Gambino tells a story about how somebody spent his money without his permission. He then goes onto list what this person bought:
- Patek refers to a Swiss luxury watch manufacturer whose products cost anywhere from a few thousand to a few million dollars.




Meanwhile, “Forty Bentley” is a reference to a highly coveted luxury car made by Bentley Motors.







Bode is a luxury menswear brand that Gambino has previously endorsed.

line: N. K. Jemisin with you, uh Got the All About Love, on some bell hooks
vault_lines: N. K. Jemisin with you, uh
meaning:
N.K. Jemisin is an African-American author who uses science fiction to discuss cultural issues and oppression.

Bino then name drops bell hooks, another black female American author, professor, feminist, and social activist.

Like Jemisin, hooks is known for her writing on race, gender, and class, discussing the difficult topics of Civil War–era (and beyond) Black writers.



Specifically, Bino mentions her 2001 novel All About Love: New Visions, which discusses aspects of love in modern society and ties in with the song’s and album’s theme.

line: Woke up in my room, she was long gone Toni singing me another sad song (Ooh)
vault_lines: Woke up in my room, she was long gone
meaning:
At the end of his escapade, Gambino wakes up alone. Forlorn, and more than likely confused by what occurred with the woman, R&B singer Toni Braxton is his only company as he plays her song, “Another Sad Love Song.”

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2yQ0Fll_9pM

Glover also makes a reference to Toni Braxton and her sad songs in the song “R.I.P.” from the mixtape Royalty:

Toni Braxton to them niggas, that’s a sad song

line: Gold mouth (Hold up, hold up), yes, I’m from the Dirty South
vault_lines: Gold mouth (Hold up, hold up), yes, I'm from the Dirty South
meaning:
Grills, or metal tooth ornaments, are a status symbol especially popular in US southern states. The Dirty South is referring to not only the region itself, but also the form of rap music that emerged in the area in the 1980s. The Dirty South style continues to influence southern artists, including Atlanta’s 21 Savage and Childish Gambino.



While 21 Savage may represent the city of Atlanta in his music, it became clear that the famous rapper is actually originally from the United Kingdom when he was arrested by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement on February 3, 2019 for overstaying his visa.

line: I’ve been countin’ M’s, me and Ben Franklin damn near kin (On God)
vault_lines: I've been counting M's, me and Ben Franklin damn near kin (On God)
meaning:
Benjamin “Ben” Franklin was a polymath scholar and one of the Founding Fathers of the United States of America. His contributions to the early stages of America’s development from English colony to country earned him a placement on the American $100 bill.

Savage feels that he is relatives or “kin” with Franklin due to the amount of time he has spent counting up his money, as each “M,” or million dollars he counts contains 10,000 $100 bills, which is a lot of Ben Franklins.

line: Pipes out (On God), all my shooters came from Moscow
vault_lines: Pipes out (On God), all my shooters came from Moscow
meaning:
21 compares his affiliates to Russian soldiers, who are known to be tough and have lethal weapons like the Russian AK-47.

21 previously shouted out Moscow on Travis Scott’s NC-17, where he raps:

Had to buy a visa, she from Moscow (21)

line: The police keep harassin’ ’cause I’m rich and I’m black (Straight up) They mad ’cause I made myself a boss without crack (On God)
vault_lines: The police keep harassin' 'cause I'm rich and I'm black (Straight up)
meaning:
Even though he has repeatedly admitted to be willing to get himself involved in high-risk, illegal activities in order to get some more money, 21 Savage has never thought about drug dealing, especially since his younger brother, Tayman, was brutally killed in a failed operation.

Plus, here he might talk about the incident that involved him in February 2019: in fact, shortly after he had released the video version of his J. Cole-assisted hit single “a lot,” which contained an extra verse on which he talked about the controversial United States' immigration policies on the country’s border with Mexico, including the forced separation of families, on February 3, 21 was arrested by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

During his incarceration, which revealed 21 had actually been born in United Kingdom, his legal team and he himself (after his eventual release) reportedly believed that the lyrics from “a lot” could have been turned by ICE into a reason to specifically target him.

The event also caused a huge discussion in the music industry, including Canadian rapper Tory Lanez releasing a special remix of “a lot” and artist like Shéyaa’s past collaborator Rich Brian addressing the event throughout the following months.

line: Dogpark looking like a Trader Joe’s (Roof, roof)
vault_lines: Dogpark looking like a Trader Joe's (Roof, roof)
meaning:
He compares the busy dog park they visit during the mushroom trip to a packed Trader Joe’s.

Trader Joe’s is a chain of discount health foods store that was first founded in Los Angeles in 1958. The chain is known having their stores packed in tight spaces, and, with the popularity the store has gotten especially with young people in recent years, the stores are often packed to the brim with customers.

line: I’m on a private jet eatin’ Popeyes chicken (21) I be flexin’ like I’m eatin’ Popeye’s spinach (21, 21, 21)
vault_lines: I'm on a private jet eatin' Popeyes chicken (21)
meaning:
21 Savage contrasts the rich lifestyle associated with flying on a private jet against eating Popeyes, a fast-food chicken restaurant that is historically associated with the South and African-American culture, whether it be through the restaurant’s Southern origins or through popular internet culture.

He, then, compares himself to the iconic cartoon sailor, Popeye, who’s arguably best known for his ability to gain muscle after eating canned spinach. 21 plays on his word “flexing” as with the Popeye mention, he’s talking about flexing his muscles and showing off his flashy lifestyle and wealth, which he exemplified by “flexing” his private jet in the line above.

line: Tracee Ellis with it when you throw back (Ooh, yeah)
vault_lines: Tracee Ellis with it when you throw back (Ooh, yeah)
meaning: Tracee Ellis Ross is an American actress and producer, known for starring in shows like Black-ish and Girlfriends. She is known to have a – let’s say – curvaceous derriere.

line: She said, “Eat this psilocybin, I’ma be right back” I’m like, “Aight” (Aight) “Ayy, I don’t know what psilocybin is” (No) “This better not be no molly” She just laughed and closed the door Dark chocolate, sea salt I took a bite She said, “We gon’ have a special night” (Ooh, ayy) I said, “Who you telling, girl? I know that”
vault_lines: She said, "Eat this psilocybin, I'ma be right back"
meaning:
Psilocybin is a naturally occuring compound found in mushrooms, hence the term “magic mushrooms” or “shrooms" being used to describe them in psychedelic culture. Though it can provide a strong euphoria, the drug has various side effects, ranging from nausea and drowsiness to an increased heart rate.

Not knowing what psilocybin is or how it affects the human brain, Gambino takes a bite of the psilocybin-laced dark chocolate candy. The girl with him, already acquainted with the potent and hallucinogenic properties of the drug, laughs at his naivety, telling him that the night will be “special.”

He mistakes her forewarning of drug-induced phantasmagoria as a sexual tease, thinking that the night will be “special” because of the lovemaking he assumes will eventually happen.
